query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: For face-centered-cubic (FCC) and body-centered-cubic (BCC) 4- to 7-component transition-metal high-entropy alloys (HEAs), a combined first-principles–trained CALPHAD surrogate can predict (i) liquidus / solidus temperature (T_m), (ii) enthalpy and entropy of fusion (ΔH_f, ΔS_f), (iii) volume change on melting (ΔV_m), and (iv) temperature-dependent liquid enthalpy and heat capacity, with mean absolute errors ≤ 30 K for T_m, ≤ 5 kJ mol⁻¹ for ΔH_f, ≤ 0.5 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ for ΔS_f, and ≤ 2 % for ΔV_m over 900–2000 K.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic or near-equiatomic (±10 at. %) FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys drawn from elements Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Al, Ti, V, Nb, Mo, Ta, W.
generation.intervention: Construct a thermodynamic surrogate by (1) generating ~10³ random quaternary-to-heptanary compositions; (2) performing DFT + machine-learned interatomic-potential molecular dynamics to compute 0 K energies and 2000–4000 K liquid enthalpies; (3) training Gaussian-process regressors on sub-lattice-wise Redlich–Kister polynomial coefficients; (4) embedding the learned parameters in a CALPHAD framework to predict melt-related properties for arbitrary compositions without further ab-initio calculations.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure (≤0.1 GPa), temperature 300-2200 K, single-phase solid solutions before melting (no intermetallics).
generation.structural_mediator: Composition-dependent excess Gibbs-energy polynomial coefficients describing the disordered FCC or BCC solid solution and the corresponding liquid solution phase.
generation.mechanism: First-principles data capture bonding and magnetic contributions to Gibbs energy; surrogate maps composition to these excess energies. CALPHAD extrapolates phase equilibria. Melting properties emerge from the crossing of the free-energy surfaces of solid and liquid phases; therefore accurate excess Gibbs energies yield accurate fusion properties and liquid-phase thermodynamics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Across the specified HEA compositional space, the surrogate will reproduce experimental or high-fidelity AIMD reference data with MAE ≤ 30 K (T_m), ≤ 5 kJ mol⁻¹ (ΔH_f), ≤ 0.5 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (ΔS_f) and ≤ 2 % (ΔV_m). Systematic deviations will remain <3× the stated MAE for ≥90 % of compositions.
generation.baseline: Conventional extrapolated binary / ternary CALPHAD databases yield errors typically 80-150 K in T_m and >10 kJ mol⁻¹ in ΔH_f for multicomponent HEAs.
generation.boundary: Fails for compositions containing >30 at.% light elements (B, C) or reactive elements (rare-earths) not in the training set, for ordered-intermetallic-forming alloys, or above 0.1 GPa where volume dependence is non-linear.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: limited experimental fusion data for multi-component HEAs; surrogate accuracy depends on representativeness of ab-initio training set and on reliability of magnetic entropy treatment.

falsification_experiment.design: Select five quinary HEAs (not used in training) spanning FCC and BCC regions (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi, AlCoCrFeNi, VNbMoTaW, TiVNbMoW, CrMnFeCoNiCu). (1) Arc-melt buttons, homogenize 1200 °C/48 h. (2) Measure melting onset, peak, and completion by containerless laser-heating DSC under Ar. (3) Measure liquid density via electrostatic levitation to 1% accuracy; derive ΔV_m. (4) Integrate DSC curves for ΔH_f and derive ΔS_f = ΔH_f/T_m. Compare to model predictions.
measurements: Density of liquid and solid at T_m (g/cm³)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mean absolute error exceeds any of: 30 K in T_m, 5 kJ mol⁻¹ in ΔH_f, 0.5 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ in ΔS_f, or 2 % in ΔV_m for more than two of the five alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.
